instruction: I find it hard to double-click quickly enough. Could you slow down the double-click speed so I have more time between clicks?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: CLICK_DELAY=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.settings-daemon.peripherals.mouse double-click 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | head -1); if [ -z "$CLICK_DELAY" ]; then CLICK_DELAY=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse double-click 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | head -1); fi; if [ -n "$CLICK_DELAY" ] && [ "$CLICK_DELAY" -ge 500 ]; then echo "Slow double-click enabled (delay: $CLICK_DELAY ms)"; else echo "Default double-click speed"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing double-click delay via Settings > Mouse > Double-Click Speed. Evaluator checks if double-click delay >= 500ms (default ~400ms). Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts double-click delay from gsettings using vm_command_line getter
Command logic properly checks both gnome.settings-daemon.peripherals.mouse (legacy) and gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse (modern) schemas with fallback
Threshold of 500ms is reasonable for 'slowed down' verification (default ~400ms)
check_include_exclude metric correctly verifies success message and excludes error cases
Minor semantic issue: evaluator checks absolute threshold (>= 500ms) rather than verifying relative increase from initial state, which means pre-existing slow settings would pass without agent action
However, without preconfig to capture initial state, the absolute threshold approach is a practical compromise
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding preconfig to capture initial double-click delay, then verify the delay was actually increased (not just >= 500ms)
Alternative: add a more conservative threshold (e.g., >= 600ms) to reduce false positives from pre-existing slow settings
